proofs.proof_tex:
The positivity premise and
\(\mathrm{lem:face\text{-}robust\text{-}tangent\text{-}score\text{-}identities}\) imply that
\(p_{n,x,h,\zeta}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) is a probability vector at every point in the support of the three-coordinate prior.  By
\(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}normalized\text{-}airy\text{-}record}\),
\(w_k^\dagger\) is a normalized, compactly supported, rational piecewise-quadratic density.  The density
\(\rho_\varepsilon\) is normalized, compactly supported, and polynomial with rational coefficients on each of its two sign intervals by its definition.  Thus the prior in
\(\mathrm{def:explicit\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}airy\text{-}tube}\) is a probability law.

Fix \(m\in\mathcal M_{n,3}\).  On a fixed rational spline piece and one of the eight sign cells, the multinomial integrand for its prior mass is
\[
\frac{n!}{\prod_t m_t!}
w_k^\dagger(x)\rho_\varepsilon(h)\rho_\varepsilon(\zeta)
\prod_{t\in\{0,1\}^3}
\left[p_{0,t}^\dagger+\alpha_n
\{xs_{x,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}
+hs_{h,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(h)}+\zeta\gamma_{0,t}\}
\right]^{m_t}.
\tag{1}
\]
Every endpoint and every coefficient other than \(\alpha_n\) in \((1)\) is rational.  Expanding the finite product and integrating its monomials exactly over the rational rectangular cell therefore gives an element of
\(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  There are finitely many spline pieces and sign cells, whence
\[
\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(m)
\in\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)
\qquad(m\in\mathcal M_{n,3}).
\tag{2}
\]
By \(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\), the orbit likelihood
\(P_m(x^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid r)\) and the exact finite-population target
\(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\) are rational.  The sums and positive-denominator quotients in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}airy\text{-}tube\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk}\) consequently show that
\[
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r),
\quad B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A},
\quad G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
\in\mathbb Q(\alpha_n).
\tag{3}
\]
All sums in \((2)\)--\((3)\) are finite because
\[
|\mathcal M_{n,3}|<\infty,
\qquad |\mathcal R_{n,3}|<\infty,
\qquad \prod_{a=1}^3(r_a+1)<\infty,
\qquad |\mathcal H(m,r,x^{\mathrm{obs}})|<\infty.
\tag{4}
\]

Here is an exact terminating comparison procedure.  Factor the square-free polynomial
\(nX^3-1\) over \(\mathbb Q\), and use the rational isolating interval for its unique positive real root to select the irreducible factor of \(\alpha_n\).  Reduce every field expression modulo that factor.  A reduced numerator is either the zero polynomial, decidable from its rational coefficients, or is nonzero at \(\alpha_n\); in the latter case repeated rational bisection of the isolating interval separates \(\alpha_n\) from every real root of that numerator and hence decides its sign.  Termination follows because two distinct real algebraic numbers have disjoint rational neighborhoods.  The additional positive algebraic numbers \(n^{1/6}\) and \(n^{1/72}\) occurring only in allocation-stratum membership are compared by the same rational root-isolation procedure.  Therefore membership in each stratum, positivity of every posterior denominator, and every finite minimum and maximum in \((3)\) are decidable.  If a stratum has no member, finite enumeration returns an emptiness certificate; otherwise comparison of its finite list returns an attaining allocation and the exact maximum.  Finally, rational bisection of
\(B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\in[0,1]\) terminates with rational endpoints
\(b^-\le b^+\) of width at most \(\delta\).

For the lower certificate,
\(\mathrm{lem:airy\text{-}tube\text{-}permutation\text{-}orbit\text{-}bayes\text{-}lower}\) applies because the positivity premise has been verified.  For every outcome-independent design and every possibly randomized labeled-data estimator, its Bayes risk under the design-independent prior is at least
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
\ge
\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
=B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{5}
\]
Maximum risk over schedules dominates the Bayes average in \((5)\).  Taking the infimum over the same design--estimator class as in
\(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\), and then using the certified lower endpoint, gives
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)
\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\ge b^-.
\tag{6}
\]

For the upper certificate, the schedule set, the observation alphabet under
\(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\), and the action grid are finite.  Every assignment probability, every observation probability \(P_y(\omega)\), every grid action, and every target value is rational.  The linear program in
\(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\) is feasible, for example by choosing any grid action and \(U=4\), because both the action and target lie in \([-1,1]\).  Its action-kernel coordinates range over a product of finite simplexes, so its objective attains a minimum; equivalently, finite enumeration of its rational basic feasible solutions returns an exact rational optimizer \((z,U)\).  The simplex constraints make \(z\) a Markov kernel into \([-1,1]\), and hence a total randomized estimator.  The remaining constraints state, separately for every fixed schedule \(y\), that this estimator's squared-error risk is at most \(U\).  The independent design \(q^\dagger\) and this estimator are feasible in the game, so
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\le U.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations \((2)\)--\((7)\) establish all of the claimed same-input outputs.  No passage to a limit in \(n\) has been used.

This proof is the algebraic and algorithmic corollary of conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) of
\(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}allocation\text{-}tube}\); it does not prove those conclusions or discharge that theorem's open uniform-expansion obligation.

Fix an input \(n\) whose diagonal admissibility flag is positive.  The root theorem gives
\[
\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le1.
\tag{1}
\]
The record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\) is a finite verified rational-interval object by
\(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}normalized\text{-}airy\text{-}record}\).  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem:corrected\text{-}airy\text{-}fixed\text{-}input\text{-}evaluator}\) with the rational width
\(\delta_n=n^{-3}\).  The positivity in \((1)\) supplies its division and probability premise, and the result is
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_n^-&\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le b_n^+,\\
0&\le b_n^+-b_n^-\le n^{-3},\\
b_n^-&\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le
\max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le U_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The lower comparison in \((2)\) is valid against every outcome-independent, possibly dependent design and every randomized labeled estimator by
\(\mathrm{lem:airy\text{-}tube\text{-}permutation\text{-}orbit\text{-}bayes\text{-}lower}\).  The upper comparison is witnessed by the returned total estimator under the admissible independent allocation \(q^\dagger\).

The definition of the exact Bayes certificate and the finiteness of
\(\mathcal R_{n,3}\) give the identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
&=n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
\mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\right\}\\
&=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The sets \(\mathcal L_n\), \(\mathcal X_n\), and \(\mathcal Z_n\) in conclusion \({\rm(A)}\) are disjoint and cover
\(\mathcal R_{n,3}\): an allocation either has a zero count, or has all counts positive and is respectively inside or outside the displayed local window.  Hence \((3)\) and the three inequalities in \({\rm(A)}\) imply
\[
n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(b_n^-\le R_n(c^\dagger)\) in \((2)\), one has
\[
D_n\le d_n^+.
\tag{5}
\]
Because
\(B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\le R_n(c^\dagger)\), equations \((3)\)--\((4)\) give
\[
D_n\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{6}
\]
Moreover, \((2)\) yields
\[
0\le
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}-b_n^-
\le b_n^+-b_n^-\le n^{-3}.
\tag{7}
\]
Combining \((3)\)--\((4)\) with \((7)\), and using
\(n^{4/3}n^{-3}=n^{-5/3}\le n^{-1}\) for \(n\ge1\), gives
\[
d_n^+
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-5/3}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-1}.
\tag{8}
\]

Let \(U_{\Lambda,n}\) be the rational upper endpoint for the Airy value in the verified record.  The evaluator definition and the root theorem give
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\le U_{\Lambda,n},
\qquad
\left[n^{4/3}(U_n-n^{-1})+U_{\Lambda,n}\right]_+
\le e_{\mathrm{pr},n}.
\tag{9}
\]
For every real \(z\), \(z\le[z]_+\).  Therefore \((9)\) implies
\[
d_n^-=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-U_n)
\ge U_{\Lambda,n}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}.
\tag{10}
\]
The relation \(R_n(c^\dagger)\le U_n\) in \((2)\) implies
\(d_n^-\le D_n\).  Together, \((5)\), \((6)\), \((8)\), and \((10)\) are exactly the two asserted finite-sample chains.

It remains to verify effectiveness uniformly over later sample sizes.  Put
\[
N_0=\max\{1,N(1,2^{-1},2^{-1})\}.
\tag{11}
\]
This is a computable integer by
\(\mathrm{lem:face\text{-}robust\text{-}tangent\text{-}score\text{-}identities}\).  For every \(n\ge N_0\), the set defining the diagonal index \(d(n)\) contains \(s=1\), so the flag is positive.  Conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) supplies a rational-valued computable nonincreasing function \(E\), a proof that \(E(N)\to0\), and the certified implication
\[
n\ge N\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N).
\tag{12}
\]
Given rational \(\eta>0\), enumerate the integers \(N\ge N_0\) and stop at the first one satisfying the decidable rational inequality
\[
E(N)+N^{-1}\le\eta.
\tag{13}
\]
The limit in \((12)\), together with \(N^{-1}\to0\), proves that this search terminates; define its output to be \(N^\dagger(\eta)\).  For any
\(n\ge N^\dagger(\eta)\), equations \((5)\), \((6)\), \((8)\), \((10)\), and \((12)\)--\((13)\) yield
\[
d_n^-\le D_n\le d_n^+,
\qquad
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-\eta\le d_n^-,D_n,d_n^+
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+\eta.
\tag{14}
\]
This is equivalent to the three required absolute-error inequalities.

Finally, diagonal mode is total by
\(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\).  On an inadmissible input it returns the deterministic zero estimator.  The contrast normalization implies
\(\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\in[-1,1]\), so that estimator has squared loss at most one and proves
\(0\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le1\).  All program data are integers, rationals, verified rational intervals, or algebraic numbers specified by rational polynomials and isolating intervals for the fixed rational contrast \(c^\dagger\).  Thus no representation, and in particular no computability assumption, for an arbitrary real contrast is used.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix integers \(n,k\ge1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and a verified spline record from
\(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\).  If
\(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\le1\), finite-input mode of \(\mathsf E\) terminates.  It returns rationals \(b^-\le b^+\) with
\[
b^-\le B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\le b^+,
\qquad b^+-b^-\le\delta,
\qquad
R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\ge b^-.
\]
For each of the local, positive-count exterior, and zero-count allocation strata in
\(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\), it returns either the exact ordered-field maximum of
\(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) when the stratum is nonempty or a certificate that the stratum is empty.  It also returns an exact rational feasible value \(U\) attained by a total procedure under the fixed independent design
\(q^\dagger\), so that \(R_n(c^\dagger)\le U\).  These are same-input finite certificates; no convergence in \(n\) is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: For n=1 both positive-count strata are empty, so the original demand for their maxima invokes an undefined maximum of the empty set. The corrected claim returns an exact maximum on a nonempty stratum and an exact emptiness certificate otherwise; all risk and evaluator conclusions are unchanged.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
The evaluator \(\mathsf E\) has finite-input and diagonal-output modes.  In finite-input mode its inputs are integers \(n,k\ge1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and the complete verified spline record returned by
\(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\).  It replays that record, constructs the rational ledger in
\(\mathrm{def:face\text{-}robust\text{-}directional\text{-}ledger}\), and verifies
\[
\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\le1.
\]
It then integrates each rational spline piece and each of the eight sign cells in
\(\mathrm{def:explicit\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}airy\text{-}tube}\), enumerates the finite sets of response counts \(m\), allocation counts \(r\), observations \(x^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and factorial tables \(H\), and evaluates every weight and posterior-risk term in the ordered field \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  It returns rationals \(b^-\le b^+\) satisfying
\[
b^-\le B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\le b^+,
\qquad b^+-b^-\le\delta,
\]
together with exact ordered-field certificates for every comparison.  For each of the three disjoint sets
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty
\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a=0\},
\end{aligned}
\]
it returns the exact maximum of
\(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) when the set is nonempty and an exact emptiness certificate otherwise.
For the attaining certificate, let \(\mathcal O_n\) be the finite observation alphabet under independent assignment with allocation \(q^\dagger\), let
\(a_j=-1+j/G\), \(0\le j\le2G\), and solve the rational linear program
\[
\begin{gathered}
\text{minimize }U\quad\text{over }(z_{\omega j},U)\quad\text{subject to}\\
z_{\omega j}\ge0,
\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{2G}z_{\omega j}=1
\quad(\omega\in\mathcal O_n),\\
\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal O_n}\sum_{j=0}^{2G}
P_y(\omega)z_{\omega j}
\{a_j-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\le U
\quad\text{for every }y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3},
\end{gathered}
\]
where \(G=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\).  The returned feasible optimizer is a total randomized estimator and \(U\) is its exact rational worst-case-risk certificate.

For diagonal mode define
\[
\overline N_s=\max_{1\le j\le s}N(j,2^{-j},2^{-j}),
\qquad
d(n)=\max\{s\le n:\overline N_s\le n\}.
\]
On input \(n\), the machine generates the records needed to decide this finite set.  If it is nonempty, it puts
\(k_n=d(n)\) and \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}=2^{-d(n)}\), calls finite-input mode, refines the Airy eigenvalue interval to width at most \(2^{-n}\), and outputs rational outward errors
\(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\),
\(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\).  The first three enclose the positive parts of the corresponding exact nonempty-set maxima minus the current lower Airy endpoint \(L_\Lambda\); when a set is empty its error is defined to be zero.  The last encloses
\[
\left[n^{4/3}\{U-n^{-1}\}+U_\Lambda\right]_+.
\]
If the set defining \(d(n)\) is empty, it reports an inadmissibility flag and returns the deterministic zero estimator.  Both modes are total.  A cross-sample certificate additionally consists of a code for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\), finite certificates that all four errors are at most \(E(N)\) whenever \(n\ge N\), and a certificate that \(E(N)\to0\).  Existence and correctness of that cross-sample extension are conclusions required of
\(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}allocation\text{-}tube}\), not inputs to the evaluator.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Finite-input mode must be total even when an allocation stratum is empty. The corrected construction specifies an emptiness certificate in that case and defines the corresponding diagonal error as zero; it leaves every nonempty-stratum computation and every risk certificate unchanged.

proposed_core_edits.name: \delta_n
proposed_core_edits.reason: The effective-certificate theorem explicitly calls finite-input mode with delta_n=n^{-3}; the frozen catalog still says n^{-3/2}. The n^{-3} width is required for the displayed scaled enclosure error n^{4/3} delta_n <= n^{-1}.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(c=c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\).  Run the diagonal Turing machine furnished by the unequal-three-arm allocation-tube theorem, and write its outputs as
\(k_n\), the verified record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\),
\(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\), \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\),
\(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\),
\(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and \(E\).  This machine terminates on every input.  Its admissibility flag is positive for every sufficiently large \(n\), and then
\[
\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le1.
\]
Put \(\delta_n=n^{-3}\).  At every such admissible input, finite-input mode of
\(\mathsf E\) terminates and returns rationals \(b_n^-\le b_n^+\), an exact rational worst-case-risk certificate \(U_n\), and a total randomized estimator
\(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) under the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\), such that
\[
b_n^-\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le b_n^+,
\qquad b_n^+-b_n^-\le\delta_n,
\qquad
b_n^-\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le
\max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
\right]\le U_n.
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
e_n^-&=\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\},\\
D_n&=n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\},\\
d_n^-&=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-U_n),
\qquad d_n^+=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-b_n^-).
\end{aligned}
\]
The returned finite certificates verify
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le d_n^-\le D_n\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-,
\qquad
D_n\le d_n^+\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-1}.
\]
The same machine returns a code and proof certificate for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\) satisfying \(E(N)\to0\) and
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N)
\qquad(n\ge N).
\]
Consequently, for every rational \(\eta>0\), a terminating search returns a computable
\(N^\dagger(\eta)\) such that, for all \(n\ge N^\dagger(\eta)\),
\[
d_n^-\le D_n\le d_n^+,
\qquad
|d_n^--\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta,
\qquad
|D_n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta,
\qquad
|d_n^+-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta.
\]
On the finite inadmissible prefix, the evaluator returns its flag and the deterministic zero estimator with the valid bracket
\(0\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le1\); hence the finite-data procedure is total for every \(n\).  No computability representation of an arbitrary real contrast is used.
proposed.justification: The proof converts the face-robust root tail and same-input exact arithmetic into certified finite risk brackets.
proposed.gap: The all-future tail is inherited from the open root; no existential analytic constant is treated as computable input.
proposed.consumer: After root closure, a planned sample size receives a terminating rational precision certificate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the stale free-symbol entry delta by the declared schedule delta_n. The mathematical claim and dependency list are unchanged, and the proof is supplied separately.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) for the face-robust three-coordinate prior.  Concretely, one must derive the exact-target Bayes-risk expansion uniformly over the local window \(\mathcal L_n\), the full positive-count exterior \(\mathcal X_n\), and every zero-count face \(\mathcal Z_n\), with a computable common tail; one must also supply a computable all-future primal tail without using the existential constant \(B_{c^\dagger}\) as program data.
open_obligations.obstruction:
The declared score identity controls Fisher information for the smooth latent mean coordinate \(\alpha_nX^\dagger\), but the loss is for the random exact finite-population target
\(M_n=\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\).  Conditional on the tube coordinates,
\(M_n-\alpha_nX^\dagger\) is a multinomial fluctuation that is observed only partially and is correlated with the arm-success counts.  For any estimator \(d(O)\), the exact decomposition
\[
\mathbb E\{d(O)-M_n\}^2
=\mathbb E\{d(O)-\alpha_nX^\dagger\}^2
+\mathbb E\{M_n-\alpha_nX^\dagger\}^2
-2\mathbb E[(d(O)-\alpha_nX^\dagger)
(M_n-\alpha_nX^\dagger)]
\]
contains a covariance term not determined by the frozen Fisher-information formula.  Indeed, the proved tangent ledger gives the exact conditional variance
\[
\operatorname{Var}(M_n\mid x,h,\zeta)
=\frac1n\left[
\alpha_n\left\{\frac58|x|+\frac3{16}|h|\right\}
-\alpha_n^2x^2\right].
\]
For bounded nonzero \(x\) or \(h\), this is of order \(n^{-4/3}\), exactly the scale of the proposed correction.  Thus the first term in the decomposition carries the leading \(n^{-1}\) risk, while the target-fluctuation variance and its covariance with the observation enter the coefficient being claimed.  Bounding the covariance separately by Cauchy--Schwarz combines an \(n^{-1}\) estimation risk with an \(n^{-4/3}\) target-fluctuation variance and gives an error of order \(n^{-7/6}\), which is larger than \(n^{-4/3}\); it therefore cannot certify the proposed coefficient.  The exact finite evaluator computes each \(n\) but proves no uniform future bound for its allocation maxima.  On the primal side, the only declared analytic remainder contains the existential \(B_{c^\dagger}\), and the current frozen core provides no explicit rational majorant from which the required program can certify an all-future modulus.  Thus neither the exact-target local coefficient nor the local/exterior/zero-face uniformity nor conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) follows from the declared primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: I rechecked the face-robust route rather than the refuted scalar tube.  The established tangent identities give the correct target derivative in the longitudinal direction, zero target derivatives for the transverse and common-shift guards, the local equalities \(H(q^\dagger)=4\), \(z(q^\dagger)=v\), and \(\beta(q^\dagger)=\gamma(q^\dagger)=0\), and proper-face directions invisible to all revealed arm marginals.  I then carried the explicit threshold ledger through the diagonal definition and proved same-input ordered-algebraic evaluation and the orbit-Bayes reduction.  I also checked the exact identity between the minimum fixed-count Bayes risk and the maximum scaled deficit.  These steps do not evaluate the posterior covariance of the random finite-population target.  Applying ordinary directional van Trees to the latent mean, or separating that covariance by Cauchy--Schwarz, loses more than the desired second-order scale.  Pointwise enumeration cannot be promoted to a computable all-future tail, and the fixed-design upper bound supplies only an unspecified finite remainder constant.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let
\[
\overline N_s=\max_{1\le j\le s}N(j,2^{-j},2^{-j}),
\qquad
d(n)=\max\{s\le n:\overline N_s\le n\}
\]
whenever the displayed set is nonempty.  For each fixed \(s\),
\(\overline N_s\) is a finite computable integer by the face-robust ledger.  If
\(n\ge\max\{s,\overline N_s\}\), then \(s\) is feasible in the definition of
\(d(n)\).  Feasibility persists when \(n\) increases, so
\[
d(n)\uparrow\infty,
\qquad k_n:=d(n)\uparrow\infty,
\qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}:=2^{-d(n)}\downarrow0.
\]
For an admissible \(n\), the definition of \(d(n)\) gives
\(n\ge N(k_n,2^{-k_n},2^{-k_n})\).  The first monotone inequality in the definition of \(N\) therefore gives
\[
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})
\le\frac12\le1.
\]
The proved fixed-input evaluator and orbit-Bayes lemma then give exact same-input values and rational enclosures and the all-procedure inequality
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)
\ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\}
=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
\]
holds exactly.  The rational-grid lemma supplies a total independent procedure and pointwise rational errors satisfying
\[
e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le(B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
This is ordinary convergence only: the frozen theorem does not expose
\(B_{c^\dagger}\) as computable data.  No declared result bounds the three allocation-stratum maxima uniformly, so none of \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) is proved by this partial result.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix integers \(n,k\geq 1\) and a rational number \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\leq 1.
\tag{1}
\]
We first identify exactly the conditional labeled experiment generated by the legacy prior.  From the definitions
\(s_x^+=\lambda_v^+-3p_0^\dagger\) and
\(s_x^-=3p_0^\dagger-\lambda_v^-\), for every real \(x\),
\[
x s_x^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}
=|x|\lambda_v^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}-3|x|p_0^\dagger;
\tag{2}
\]
the choice of sign at \(x=0\) is immaterial.  The analogous identity following from
\(s_h^+=\lambda_d^+-2p_0^\dagger\) and
\(s_h^-=2p_0^\dagger-\lambda_d^-\) is
\[
h s_h^{\operatorname{sign}(h)}
=|h|\lambda_d^{\operatorname{sign}(h)}-2|h|p_0^\dagger.
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently, the restriction \(\zeta=0\) in
\(\mathrm{def:scalar\text{-}airy\text{-}tube\text{-}legacy}\) has response probabilities
\[
p_{n,x,h,0,t}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
=p_{0,t}^\dagger+
\alpha_n\left\{|x|\lambda_{v,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}
+|h|\lambda_{d,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(h)}
-(3|x|+2|h|)p_{0,t}^\dagger\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]
This is the two-coordinate fiber in
\(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\).  Since
\(|x|\leq T_k^\dagger\), \(|h|\leq\varepsilon\), and (1) holds, that proposition proves that (4) is a probability distribution on the eight response types.

Conditional on \((X^\dagger,H^\dagger)=(x,h)\), the construction draws the count vector \(m\) multinomially from (4) and then draws a labeled response-type sequence uniformly in its count orbit.  For a labeled sequence \((t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) with counts \(m=(m_t)_t\), its conditional probability is therefore
\[
\left\{\frac{n!}{\prod_t m_t!}
\prod_t\bigl(p_{n,x,h,0,t}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\bigr)^{m_t}\right\}
\left\{\frac{\prod_t m_t!}{n!}\right\}
=\prod_{i=1}^n p_{n,x,h,0,t_i}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus the labeled types are conditionally independent and identically distributed with law (4).

Consider the deterministic allocation count \(r=(n,0,0)\).  Every unit is assigned to arm one.  The estimator
\[
\widetilde\tau_n
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)
=\frac{2X_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{n}-1
\tag{6}
\]
is therefore a function of the observed data.  Define
\[
e(t)=2t_1-1-(c^\dagger)^\top t.
\tag{7}
\]
The finite-population identity in
\(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\) gives, for every labeled sequence with count vector \(m\),
\[
\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n e(t_i).
\tag{8}
\]
Because \(2t_1-1=2(b_t)_1\), while the same proposition gives
\(\mathbb E[b_t\mid x,h]=\alpha_n(xv+hd^\dagger)\) and
\(\mathbb E[(c^\dagger)^\top t\mid x,h]=\alpha_nx\), we obtain, using
\(v_1=1/2\) and \(d_1^\dagger=0\),
\[
\mathbb E[e(t)\mid x,h]
=2\alpha_n(xv_1+hd_1^\dagger)-\alpha_nx=0.
\tag{9}
\]

In lexicographic order \(000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111\), direct substitution of
\(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) into (7) gives
\[
\bigl(e(t)^2\bigr)_t
=\left(1,\frac1{16},\frac9{16},0,0,
\frac9{16},\frac1{16},1\right).
\tag{10}
\]
Since \(p_0^\dagger=(\delta_{000}+\delta_{111})/2\), it follows that
\[
\sum_t p_{0,t}^\dagger e(t)^2=1.
\tag{11}
\]
Using the four response measures displayed in the frozen core and (10), for either sign we have
\[
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^{\pm}e(t)^2
=1+\frac9{16}+\frac1{16}=\frac{13}{8},
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^{\pm}e(t)^2
=\frac{23}{16}.
\tag{12}
\]
For completeness, the second equality is, for the positive measure,
\[
\frac34\frac9{16}+\frac34\cdot1
+\frac14\frac1{16}+\frac14\cdot1=\frac{23}{16},
\tag{13}
\]
and the negative measure has the same four squared-error values with the same weights.  Substitution of (11)--(12) into (4) now yields the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E[e(t)^2\mid x,h]
&=1+\alpha_n\left\{
|x|\left(\frac{13}{8}-3\right)
+|h|\left(\frac{23}{16}-2\right)\right\}\\
&=1-\alpha_n\left(\frac{11}{8}|x|+\frac9{16}|h|\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
Combining conditional independence from (5), the zero mean (9), and the target identity (8), we get
\[
\mathbb E\left[
(\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m))^2\mid x,h\right]
=\frac1n\left\{1-\alpha_n\left(
\frac{11}{8}|x|+\frac9{16}|h|\right)\right\}.
\tag{15}
\]

Under the scalar prior the two coordinates are independent, with densities \(w_k^\dagger\) and \(\rho_\varepsilon\).  The declared formula for the latter gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_{\mathbb R}|h|\rho_\varepsilon(h)\,dh
&=\frac{30}{16\varepsilon}\int_0^\varepsilon
h\left(1-\frac{h^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^2\,dh\\
&=\frac{30\varepsilon}{16}\int_0^1u(1-u^2)^2\,du
=\frac5{16}\varepsilon.
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]
Since \(\alpha_n=n^{-1/3}\), integrating (15) proves that the Bayes risk of the observable estimator (6) equals
\[
\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left\{
\frac{11}{8}\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
+\frac{45}{256}\varepsilon\right\}.
\tag{17}
\]
For every observation value with positive prior-predictive probability and every action \(a\), conditional square completion gives
\[
\mathbb E[(a-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m))^2\mid X^{\mathrm{obs}}]
=\operatorname{Var}(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\mid X^{\mathrm{obs}})
+\left\{a-\mathbb E[\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\mid X^{\mathrm{obs}}]\right\}^2.
\tag{18}
\]
Hence the posterior mean used in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}scalar\text{-}airy\text{-}tube\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk}\) minimizes conditional risk; zero-probability observation values contribute nothing.  Because (6) is an admissible observed-data action, (17)--(18) imply
\[
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
\leq \frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left\{
\frac{11}{8}\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
+\frac{45}{256}\varepsilon\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
Applying the definition of
\(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}\) to (19) proves
\[
G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
\geq
\frac{11}{8}\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
+\frac{45}{256}\varepsilon.
\tag{20}
\]

It remains to evaluate the limiting longitudinal moment.  Put
\(\kappa=\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\),
\(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\),
\(A=\int_{\mathbb R}|\Phi'|^2\), and
\(B=\int_{\mathbb R}|x|\Phi^2\).  The scaling
\(f(x)=\kappa^{1/6}g(\kappa^{1/3}x)\) preserves the \(L^2\) norm and gives
\[
4\int|f'|^2+\kappa\int|x|f^2
=\kappa^{2/3}\left\{4\int|g'|^2+\int|x|g^2\right\}.
\tag{21}
\]
Thus the definitions of \(C_A\), \(\Phi\), and \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\) imply
\[
4A+\kappa B=C_A\kappa^{2/3}=\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\tag{22}
\]
For \(s>0\), let \(\Phi_s(x)=s^{1/2}\Phi(sx)\).  It also has unit \(L^2\) norm, and its energy is
\[
E(s)=4s^2A+\kappa s^{-1}B.
\tag{23}
\]
Because \(\Phi\) is the ground-state minimizer in
\(\mathrm{def:airy\text{-}benchmark}\), \(s=1\) minimizes (23).  Differentiation at this interior point gives
\[
0=E'(1)=8A-\kappa B.
\tag{24}
\]
Solving (22)--(24) and using \(\kappa=5/8\) gives
\[
B=\frac{2\Lambda_{c^\dagger}}{3\kappa}
=\frac{16}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\tag{25}
\]

By \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}normalized\text{-}airy\text{-}record}\),
\(\varphi_k^\dagger\to\Phi\) in weighted \(H^1\).  In particular,
\(Z_k:=\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2\to1\).  Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|\int |x|\{(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2-\Phi^2\}\,dx\right|
&\leq
\left(\int |x||\varphi_k^\dagger-\Phi|^2\,dx\right)^{1/2}\\
&\quad\times
\left(\int |x||\varphi_k^\dagger+\Phi|^2\,dx\right)^{1/2}
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
The second factor is bounded because
\(|\varphi_k^\dagger+\Phi|^2\leq
2|\varphi_k^\dagger-\Phi|^2+8|\Phi|^2\), weighted convergence holds, and \(B<\infty\).  Since
\(w_k^\dagger=(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2/Z_k\), equations (25)--(26) prove
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
\longrightarrow \frac{16}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\tag{27}
\]

Now let \(k_n\to\infty\) and let the positive rational sequence \(\varepsilon_n\) satisfy the admissibility condition in the statement.  The transverse term in (20) is nonnegative, so (20) and (27) yield
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
\geq \frac{11}{8}\frac{16}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}
=\frac{22}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\tag{28}
\]
The definition of \(C_A\) and the proved value \(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8>0\) give
\(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}>0\); hence the last member of (28) is strictly larger than \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).

Finally, \((n,0,0)\in\mathcal R_{n,3}\) has zero coordinates.  If a sequence
\(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\to0\) satisfied the asserted upper bound for every allocation count with a zero coordinate, applying it to \((n,0,0)\) would make the left side of (28) at most \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  This contradicts (28), and proves the final assertion.
